content:
Liam: Heads up — seeing 2–3x 95/99th tail latency on Mixtral-MoE routes since last runtime deploy (v2.4.1). Spikes concentrate on 2 shards and correlate with the same expert set. Logs show router logits peaking and then a big queue on certain expert workers.

Nina: Any profiler snapshots? nvprof/torchprof would help.

Liam: Pasted quick profiler summary from a repro run: 
```
Profile summary:
- Router forward: 12.8ms (avg) -> spikes to ~120ms on tail
- Expert dispatch (hot experts): 80ms queue observed
- Kernel selection: falls back to generic_gemm on long seq paths (~30% of calls)
- KV cache lookups: 3.4ms per token on misses, cache hit ratio dropped to 62% during spike
```

perf-bot: GPU0 util 95% | GPU1 util 88% | Mem 18.9/24GB | 95th latency 420ms -> tail 980ms (rolling 5m)

Devin: Hypothesis: top_k routing + router logits temperature amplifies load imbalance. Also the kernel selector might pick a slower codepath when topk causes variable sequence padding across microbatches. Quick trials to try: top_k=2, router_temp=0.8, batcher.max_batch_size=16, kernel_hint=fused_attn for seq < 1024.

Ara: I noticed expert_cache_pressure currently set to 0.7 in the canary profile — that's pretty aggressive. Lowering to 0.4 reduces eviction churn and should cut KV miss rate. Also try bumping expert_parallelism to 12 to provide more dispatch lanes.

Chris: Also check RoPE scaling — if rope_scale differs between training and this inference config, attention magnitudes change and router logits can skew. On one customer run we saw rope_scale=1.0 in model config but runtime default 0.98 which changed head activation distribution. That can shift which experts get high scores.

Liam: Repro plan: create a canary with these changes: top_k=2, router_temp=0.9, expert_parallelism=12, expert_cache_pressure=0.4, kernel_hint=fused_attn. Run 5% traffic for 1h with detailed traces and per-expert histograms. I'll run profiler snapshots at +30m and +50m.

Devin: Add a runtime guard: if any expert queue latency > 200ms for > 10s, fallback that request to dense_mixtral path. Example config snippet: 
```json
{"routing": {"top_k": 2, "temp": 0.9, "fallback": "dense_mixtral"}}
```

Nina: Please also emit router_logits entropy per-request and a per-expert request counter. Low entropy -> concentrated routing -> alert threshold.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled: svc/mixtral-moe -> traffic 5% at 2026-03-18T15:10Z. Canary id=canary-1127. Tracing enabled.

Liam: I'll collect nvprof + PyTorch profiler on canary pods. @Ara can you own the KV cache telemetry dashboard and add a panel for evictions/min and hit ratio?

Ara: On it. I'll also push a small test build that toggles rope_scale to 0.98 vs 1.0 to see effect.

Chris: If these config changes don't reduce tail, next step: force deterministic uniform routing (hash-based) for a subset to separate router model skew vs true expert hotness. If uniform reduces tail, the router model is the problem; otherwise it's expert capacity.

Devin: I'll prepare the rollout script + automated rollback (traffic -> 0% on >2x baseline error or >2x tail latency).

Liam: Action items: Devin - rollout & rollback; Ara - KV/dashboard + cache param change & rope toggle; Nina - router entropy histograms; Chris - verify model rope config & heads/kv dims parity; me - profiler + traces. Reconvene in 60m with first traces. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment canary-1127 started on cluster-prod (pods: mixtral-moe-canary-3).

perf-bot: First 10m metrics: avg latency down 8% on canary but tail still high (95th 410ms -> 95th 430ms). Expert queue histogram attached to dashboard.

Liam: Thanks — sharing profiler when ready. If we see per-expert hotspots persist despite top_k=2, we'll try the deterministic routing test next.
